description:
Apply per-user DEK encryption to user_flags and subscriptions. These tables reveal reading habits (which articles a user has read, which newsgroups they follow) which qualify as personal data under GDPR.

## user_flags
  Columns: (user_id, article_cid BYTEA, seen INT, flagged INT)
  article_cid is a CID — not sensitive, but (user_id, article_cid) together
  reveals reading history. Encrypt the row value, not the key.

  Options:
  A. Encrypt article_cid as the 'value' column: makes the read-state opaque
     but prevents indexed lookup by article_cid. Requires full table scan
     per user to find flags for a specific article.
  B. Store article_cid plaintext, encrypt a 'flags_blob BYTEA' column that
     contains (seen, flagged) encrypted. Preserves indexed lookup; only the
     flag values are protected.

  Recommendation: Option B. The article_cid is a public CID (not secret);
  only the fact that this user has read it is sensitive. Encrypt the flags
  blob, keep the lookup key plaintext. This is a pragmatic tradeoff.

  Schema change:
    ALTER TABLE user_flags
        ADD COLUMN flags_blob BYTEA,
        DROP COLUMN seen,
        DROP COLUMN flagged;
  (flags_blob = AES-256-GCM encrypt of JSON {"seen":bool,"flagged":bool})

## subscriptions
  Columns: (user_id, group_name TEXT, subscribed_at BIGINT)
  group_name reveals which newsgroups the user reads. Encrypt group_name.

  Schema change:
    ALTER TABLE subscriptions
        ALTER COLUMN group_name TYPE BYTEA USING group_name::BYTEA;

  Impact: subscription lookups currently do WHERE group_name = ?.
  After encryption, lookups must fetch all rows for user_id and decrypt
  client-side. For typical subscription counts (10–500 groups) this is
  acceptable. If it becomes a bottleneck, a deterministic HMAC index
  (HMAC-SHA256(DEK, group_name)) can be added alongside the ciphertext
  for O(1) lookup without revealing plaintext.

## Acceptance
  - user_flags.flags_blob is ciphertext in DB for new writes
  - subscriptions.group_name is ciphertext in DB for new writes
  - Existing read paths (UserFlagsStore, subscription queries) return correct values after decryption
  - Performance: 500 subscriptions decrypted in < 5ms (AES-GCM is fast; this is a sanity check)
title: Encrypt user_flags and subscriptions rows under per-user DEK
